title: Israel's Watergen produces drinking water from the air: from soldiers at the front to a hospital in Gaza

trailer.text: Watergen is an Israeli company that produces drinking water from the humidity in the air, and CBN News describes it as a world leader in the field.
According to AFP, Russian-Israeli billionaire Michael Mirilashvili, an Israeli citizen and observant Jew, bought the company.
The machines reached an orphanage in Uzbekistan, hurricane victims in the USA, and also Gaza, where some of the water goes to a hospital for kidney patients.

glance.label: Scope
glance.value: More than 60 or more than 80 countries, depending on the source

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: TIME: one of the best inventions of 2019, according to the company's website

stations.title: Water for soldiers on the front line

paragraphs.text: According to Dezeen, during his service in the IDF, Arye Kohavi saw that soldiers on the front line were sometimes left without water when convoys were destroyed.
So he designed a device that produces drinking water in combat zones.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the Israeli founders initially thought of using the technology to reduce the power consumption of home appliances.

stations.title: A new owner: water for every person

paragraphs.text: According to AFP, Michael Mirilashvili is a Russian-Israeli billionaire, an Israeli citizen and observant Jew.
According to AFP, he bought Watergen after moving to Israel in 2009.
According to Mirilashvili, the goal was to supply drinking water to every person on Earth.
As company president, he said that Watergen can not only save millions, but also improve the lives of billions.
AFP: after he moved to Israel in 2009, with no exact year

stations.title: How water comes out of the air

paragraphs.text: According to AFP, the machine captures humidity from the air, condenses it into water and filters it into drinking water that can be drunk immediately.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the air goes through a heat exchange and cooling process called GENius and condenses into water.
According to Euronews, the generators work like dehumidifiers.
According to AFP and Euronews, the amount of water depends on the air's humidity.
According to Dezeen, the large modules are enough for hospitals, schools or even an entire village.
According to Euronews, the generators are suitable for remote villages and also for private homes in the city.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the large generator needs only a standard electricity supply, with no additional infrastructure.
Euronews wrote that the technology seeks to solve the chronic water crisis in the Gaza Strip.
According to the United Nations, only three percent of the water in Gaza meets international standards.
The aquifer has been overused and damaged by seawater and pollution, so most of the water is salty and dangerous to drink.
Multiple studies have linked the poor water to a rise in kidney stones and a high rate of diarrhea.
According to Euronews, after the Hamas takeover in 2007 the border was blockaded by Israel, power cuts increased water contamination, and so residents buy water from local vendors.
According to a UNICEF estimate, two-thirds of this water is already contaminated by the time it reaches the consumer.
Many players are trying to help, including the European Union, which is supporting a large seawater desalination plant.
According to Mirilashvili, when he learned about the water crisis in Gaza, he immediately wanted to help.
According to him, it was immediately clear that the neighbors had to be helped first.
According to AFP, the technology is suited to Gaza because it runs on solar panels, and the only power plant there does not meet demand.
According to AFP, Israel tightly controls imports to Gaza, and Mirilashvili acknowledged that getting the machines approved "took some time".
According to him, the army "liked the idea", but needed to check the equipment.
According to Euronews, it took him a year to get permission, and he succeeded in bringing three machines into Gaza.
According to AFP, Watergen donated two machines, each costing $61 thousand.
According to AFP, the third machine was sent by the Arava Institute for Environmental Studies, on a kibbutz in southern Israel.
According to AFP, Israeli companies cannot operate in Gaza, so the Palestinian group Damour operates one of the machines.
According to Euronews, the generators were installed in hospitals and public places for people in need.
One of the machines is located at the town hall in Khan Yunis.
According to Khalil of the Damour group, some of the water is drunk by town hall employees, and some goes to a local hospital for kidney patients.
According to AFP, engineer Nadia Tubail checked filters on the solar-powered generator in Khan Yunis on 16 November 2020.
Asked about working with an Israeli company, Khalil said that they accept help from anyone who wants to help.
Mirilashvili said that the water is a gift from God, and that the Gazans understood that when God gives something, it must be accepted.
According to JNS, the water supply in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, was cut off for almost two days, and the city was left without drinking water.
According to JNS, Watergen supplied drinking water to more than 120 children in an orphanage in the city.
According to Mirilashvili, although the air humidity in Bukhara is only 20 percent, the GEN-350 machine produced hundreds of liters of high-quality drinking water.
According to Michael Rutman of Watergen, the children were very excited to drink the water.
According to the Times of Central Asia, on 29 October 2019 the government of Uzbekistan and Watergen signed a memorandum of understanding.
According to the memorandum, thousands of generators will be sent to cities and towns facing water shortages, including Bukhara and Samarkand.
Uzbekistan's deputy prime minister said that the country desperately needs technology such as Watergen's.

stations.title: From hurricanes in the USA to a boarding school in Colombia

paragraphs.text: According to Dezeen, in 2017 Watergen assisted after hurricanes Irma and Harvey in the USA, and in New Delhi it supplied free water to 2,000 people a day for a month.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the system also assisted during the 2018 California wildfires.
According to Watergen's website, in Kerala, India, after the 2018 floods, a generator that arrived through the TATA Trust supplies water to 200 to 300 people every day.
According to the Jerusalem Post, in January 2019 Watergen announced a partnership with the Red Cross on an emergency vehicle that will bring water to disaster zones.
According to Michael Rotman of Watergen, hospitals are increasingly turning to the company because of the water quality.
According to Watergen's website, in Cambodia generators operate in hospitals, and in Colombia two units supply water to 1,500 Wayuu students at a boarding school.
According to the company's website, in South Africa the organization World Vision operates a trailer-mounted generator, as a water point that comes to the people.

According to CBN News, after the Abraham Accords Mirilashvili came to the United Arab Emirates, and according to Michael Rutman, co-CEO at Watergen, the company's machines are installed all over Abu Dhabi.
According to CBN News, a cornerstone was laid there for a Watergen factory.
According to Watergen's website, TIME magazine named the GENNY system one of the best inventions of 2019.
According to the company's website, in 2018 the World Economic Forum selected Watergen as a Technology Pioneer.
According to the company's website, Frost & Sullivan named it one of the world's 50 most innovative companies.
According to AFP, only a few machines operate in Gaza, and Watergen is far from meeting the need of two million residents.
Khalil told AFP that one or two machines will not change anything, but they show that there is a solution.
Mirilashvili lamented that he cannot see his machines at work, because Israelis are forbidden from entering the strip.
According to AFP, Hamas did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Mirilashvili said that the greatest problem is that the company cannot supply the growing demand.
According to AFP, Watergen's CEO and president, Mirilashvili, was held in prison in Russia after a kidnapping conviction, in a trial that the European Court of Justice later found was flawed.
According to AFP, the European Court of Justice later found that the trial was flawed.

claims.quote: In light of Uzbekistan’s water shortage, Uzbekistan desperately needs technology such as that provided by Watergen in order to improve its water sector

claims.quote: It has also assisted rescue and recovery efforts during the 2018 California wildfires and provided clean water to the residents of Texas and Florida in the aftermath of the devastation caused by Hurricanes Harvey and Irma.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, בקרלה שבהודו, אחרי שיטפונות 2018, מחולל גדול שהגיע דרך קרן טאטא מספק מים ל-200 עד 300 איש מדי יום.
claims.quote: When the 2018 floods contaminated the sources around Parumala Seminary, a large-scale unit arrived through the TATA Trust — and 200 to 300 people have drawn water from it daily ever since.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בינואר 2019 ווטרגן הודיעה על שיתוף פעולה עם הצלב האדום לפיתוח רכב חירום שיספק מים לאזורי אסון קשים.
claims.quote: In January 2019, Watergen announced that it had partnered with the Red Cross to develop a new Emergency Response Vehicle (ERV) for providing fresh water to even the most challenging disaster zones.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, בקמבודיה מחוללי GEN-M פועלים בבתי חולים ומספקים עד 800 ליטר מי שתייה ביום כל אחד.
claims.quote: GEN-M units stand at Calmette Hospital and at Kantha Bopha, Cambodia’s largest public children’s hospital — each providing up to 800 liters of drinking water a day.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, בקולומביה שתי יחידות מספקות מי שתייה ל-1,500 תלמידי וואיו בפנימייה.
claims.quote: In Colombia’s driest department, two GEN-M units supply the San Antonio de Aremasain boarding school with clean drinking water for 1,500 Wayuu students

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, בדרום אפריקה ארגון וורלד ויז'ן מפעיל מחולל GEN-M על נגרר, כנקודת מים ניידת שמגיעה אל האנשים.
claims.quote: In an underserved district of Port Elizabeth, where the few clean sources are overstressed, World Vision South Africa runs a trailer-mounted GEN-M

claims.text: לפי CBN News, אחרי חתימת הסכמי אברהם הגיע מירילשוילי לאבו דאבי, ולדבריו מכונות החברה מותקנות בכל רחבי העיר.
claims.quote: We started here, almost six months ago, and today, our machines are installed all over Abu Dhabi

claims.text: לפי CBN News, הונחה אבן פינה למפעל ייצור של ווטרגן באיחוד האמירויות.
claims.quote: Another major announcement came with laying the cornerstone for a Watergen production facility in the UAE.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, החברה נבחרה ב-2018 לחלוצת טכנולוגיה של הפורום הכלכלי העולמי.
claims.quote: Watergen selected as a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, החברה נבחרה בידי Frost & Sullivan לאחת מ-50 החברות החדשניות בעולם.
claims.quote: Watergen named among the World’s 50 Most Innovative Companies by Frost & Sullivan.

claims.text: AFP כתבה שבעזה פועלות רק מעט מכונות, ולכן ווטרגן רחוקה מלענות על הביקוש של שני מיליון תושבים.
claims.quote: With just a few machines operating in Gaza, Watergen is far from meeting demand for the two million people who live in the crowded coastal enclave wedged between Israel, Egypt and the Mediterranean Sea.

claims.text: חאלד אמר ל-AFP שמכונה או שתיים לא ישנו דבר, אך הן מראות שיש פתרון.
claims.quote: One or two machines won’t change anything,” he told AFP. But “it shows there is a solution”.

claims.text: מירילשוילי התלונן שאינו יכול לראות את מכונותיו בפעולה, כי ישראלים אסורים בכניסה לרצועה.
claims.quote: Mirilashvili lamented that he cannot see his machines at work, as Israelis are forbidden from entering the strip.

claims.text: לפי AFP, חמאס לא הגיב מיד לבקשת תגובה.
claims.quote: Hamas did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, מירילשוילי אמר שהבעיה הגדולה ביותר היא שהחברה אינה מצליחה לספק את הביקוש הגדל.
claims.quote: Our greatest problem is that we cannot supply the growing demand,” said Mirilashvili.

claims.text: לפי AFP, מנכ"ל ווטרגן ריצה זמן בכלא רוסי בעקבות הרשעה בחטיפה, במשפט שבית הדין האירופי לצדק מצא אחר כך שהיה פגום.
claims.quote: The company CEO and president has a colorful personal history, including time spent in a Russian prison following a kidnapping conviction in a trial the European Court of Justice later found was flawed.

claims.text: לפי כיתוב תמונה של AFP, מירילשוילי נפגש עם AFP במשרדיו בפתח תקווה.
claims.quote: talks to AFP at his offices in the Israeli city of Petah Tikva, on November 17, 2020.

claims.text: לפי AFP, משרדי ווטרגן נמצאים במגדל זכוכית בתל אביב, כ-80 ק"מ צפונית לעזה.
claims.quote: Watergen’s offices are located in a glass tower in Tel Aviv, some 80 kilometers (50 miles) north of Gaza.

claims.text: לפי JNS, ה-GEN-350 שוקל 780 ק"ג וניתן להתקנה בקלות.
claims.quote: With a weight of just 780 kg. (1,700 pounds), the GEN-350 is transportable and can be installed easily.

claims.text: לפי אלגמיינר/JNS, ה-GEN-350 שוקל 800 ק"ג וניתן להתקנה בקלות.
claims.quote: With a weight of just 800 kilograms, the GEN-350 is transportable and can be installed easily.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, ווטרגן מפיקה מי שתייה ב-250 ואט-שעה לליטר בלבד, כשני עד ארבעה סנט לליטר.
claims.quote: Watergen produces safe drinking water at only 250Wh/L – or, in financial terms, a mere two to four cents per liter.

claims.text: לפי CleanTechnica, יחידות ווטרגן צורכות 200 ואט-שעה לליטר מים.
claims.quote: Watergen’s units consume 200 watt-hours per liter of water generated or 1 kilowatt-hours of power for 5 liters of water.

claims.text: לפי אתר ווטרגן, בדצמבר 2019 נחנך מחולל GEN-M בבניין העירייה בעבסאן אל-כבירה, מחולל המים מאוויר הראשון בעזה, שהוצג בשיתוף מכון ערבה ושותפים פלסטינים.
claims.quote: In December 2019, a GEN-M was inaugurated in the town’s municipal building — the first atmospheric water generator in Gaza, introduced with the Arava Institute and its Palestinian partners.

claims.text: לפי חאלד מארגון דמור, כשלחות האוויר מעל 65 אחוזים המכונות מפיקות כ-5,000 ליטר ביום.
claims.quote: When the air’s humidity level is above 65 percent, Watergen’s machines can produce about 5,000 liters of drinking water per day, said Khalil of the Palestinian group Damour.

claims.text: לפי מיכאל רוטמן מווטרגן, בתי חולים פונים יותר ויותר לחברה בגלל המים המושלמים שהמכונות מפיקות.
claims.quote: Michael shared that hospitals are increasingly coming to Watergen for their products because of the perfect water they generate.
The innovation—and the company—dates to 2009

claims.text: בעלים: מיכאל מירילשוילי
claims.quote: which was acquired by Israeli-Georgian businessman Michael Mirilashvili in 2016
